definitions.explanation: From English "town". Rarely used alone; it appears in loanword compounds for kinds of towns and for local things.

examples.japanese: タウン{誌|し}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}む→読む：00426_yomu⟧。
examples.english: To read a local town magazine.

examples.japanese: ⟦{駅前|えきまえ}→駅前：09593_ekimae⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{商店街|しょうてんがい}→商店街：09391_shoutengai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧「⟦{学生|がくせい}→学生：00610_gakusei⟧タウン」⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{呼|よ}ばれている→呼ぶ：00766_yobu⟧。
examples.english: The shopping street in front of the station is called "Student Town".

examples.japanese: ⟦{郊外|こうがい}→郊外：01403_kougai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ニュータウン⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{同|おな}じ→同じ：02857_onaji⟧⟦{頃|ころ}→頃：32850_koro⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}して→引っ越す：01171_hikkosu⟧きた⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: In the suburban new town, many families moved in at about the same time.

notes:
USAGE:
- For "town" on its own, say ⟦{町|まち}→町：00613_machi⟧

COMPOUNDS:
- ニュータウン: a planned new town
- タウン{誌|し}: a local magazine about a town's shops and events
- ベッドタウン: a commuter town (a Japanese coinage; English says bedroom community)
- ゴーストタウン: ghost town
- ダウンタウン: downtown
